# hrc-runtime — Active Invariants

## hrc-runtime.acp-event-bridge

An enabled HRC event bridge observes only committed, allowlisted reason-coded facts and emits the frozen schema-v1 ACP envelope with node-qualified event identity, recorded initiating origin and causation, and a pointer-only payload. Producer emission is durably rate-bounded, runs after commit without affecting the originating write, and is best-effort rather than a second source of truth. V1 activation is disabled by default and confined to the HRC node co-resident with the ACP listener; payload node identity is provenance and a fail-loud tripwire, not execution-routing authority.

## hrc-runtime.architecture-law

Durable HRC architecture laws are stored as machine-checked records with explicit authority, source evidence, required tests, and reopen triggers.

## hrc-runtime.asp-toolchain-selection

Every HRC-owned ASP child spawn resolves its binary at spawn time through one selection authority. A non-empty per-binary command override wins, then the binary's canonical name under an explicitly configured absolute HRC_ASP_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, then the HRC release's resolveHoistedBinary result. No spawn path, including the legacy interactive stdio broker path, independently selects or caches a command; injected constant commands are test seams only. A configured-root selection that is missing or not executable fails before spawn, and incompatible facade or broker protocol/capability hellos fail closed before invocation work. Admin status derives effective source and path from the same resolver and distinguishes them from the immutable bundled ASP tuple governed by hrc-runtime.observable-release. The root is one configuration namespace, not an atomic build-identity boundary, and the daemon's in-process ASP imports remain pinned to its release.

## hrc-runtime.bounded-lifecycle-event-observation

HRC owns the lifecycle ledger incarnation and canonical event envelope. Its bounded tail returns the selected ascending page, global head, and incarnation from one transaction. An exclusive-before reverse page requires its expected incarnation, rejects replacement with cursor_invalid and no events, applies exact host-session and generation filters before its descending limit-plus-one read, and reverses only the admitted page to chronological order. Existing head callers that omit the reverse cursor retain their behavior. Its bounded follow stream requires an expected incarnation plus exclusive sequence, atomically admits and pins that ledger incarnation, admits no replacement-ledger event, and orders advisory ready, explicit gap, and canonical event records. Replay, seam, and live admission remain within fixed row and serialized-byte ceilings and are pulled through a one-record transport handoff. Ready is not resumable progress; only a fully received event or gap advances a consumer cursor. This observation contract is distinct from and does not amend hrc-runtime.acp-event-bridge.

## hrc-runtime.bounded-state-retention-writes

A fresh HRC database selects incremental auto-vacuum before journal setup or migration DDL. An existing database whose effective auto-vacuum mode is not incremental remains fail-closed for retention deletes until a coordinated offline full VACUUM installs the pointer map. Each retention batch completes full-predicate candidate discovery as a read before any write begins. The subsequent DELETE receives no more than the adaptive batch size of selected integer primary keys through one bounded JSON set, searches target rows by primary key, and re-evaluates the complete eligibility and terminal/live safety predicate inside the write transaction. Discovery may traverse an arbitrarily large eligible range without writer authority; target-table scan work under the writer is forbidden and bounded-key virtual-table scan work is permitted. The deadline is checked again between discovery and deletion, and concurrent state changes may reduce the deleted count without widening the writer's candidate universe.

## hrc-runtime.canonical-package-publication

Every canonical HRC package set is produced from one clean commit contained by a freshly fetched named canonical ref, carries the exact normative praesidiumBuild tuple, refuses same-name/version replacement, and is verified by cache-empty registry tarball reads before publication succeeds.

## hrc-runtime.collaboration-auto-reply-actuation

When one runtime turn is driven by presentation of exactly one pending wrkq envelope, or one fan-out group from one sender, successful turn completion and a non-empty canonical dispatcher response establish an automatic-reply obligation. The same durable local transaction that completes the drive attempt records one bodyless pending intent containing its driveAttemptId, envelope or group identity, room, counterparty, and runId. The body is the exact canonical turn-response projection produced by the shared finalizeSemanticTurnResponse path, including its established ordered concatenation, TURN_TEXT_LIMIT truncation, and truncation marker; the reconciler derives it from the durable run events and never stores a second copy. The reconciler first reads the presented envelope's authoritative wrkq discharge state. A discharged envelope terminates the intent as already-discharged. Otherwise it emits one ordinary say from the exact agent principal at seat scope to the originating room and counterparty, carrying idempotency key auto-reply:<driveAttemptId> and auto: turn_final provenance. Confirmed success terminates the intent as minted. Every other write outcome, including timeout, lost response, crash and replay, and wrkq's duplicate-key refusal, is resolved by reading the existing authoritative wrkq envelope surface for a committed envelope from that principal with the exact idempotency key. A matching row is the mint receipt and terminates the intent as minted; a successful read with no match leaves the intent retryable. A read failure supplies no absence proof and leaves the intent pending. The idempotency key is correlation and duplicate exclusion, never a replay receipt. HRC's pending row is actuation bookkeeping only and is not room, envelope, obligation, discharge, or reply-body authority. A failed runtime turn records no pending automatic reply. A successful turn with an empty canonical response records the terminal empty-response outcome, emits no synthetic content, and leaves the envelope in its existing undisposed lifecycle. Drives spanning multiple senders or rooms do not enter this automatic path. An automatically minted ordinary say has exactly the existing reply-is-ack and counterparty-obligation semantics. Driven-turn priming treats the turn response as the reply; explicit wrkc say remains for other rooms or counterparties, mid-turn communication, and FYI closure. The discharge read and ordinary say are intentionally non-atomic by principal ruling. A manual say that commits between them may therefore be followed by the automatic reply; that duplicate window is the accepted risk wrkq.collaboration-ledger.auto-reply-manual-race and is not an exactly-once claim. No conditional wrkq mutation, new wrkq write surface, say error mapping, or RoomSayParams contract is introduced.

## hrc-runtime.collaboration-state-retention

messages, collective_history_messages, collective_history_observations, collective_history_replications, and every hrcmail_* table are keep-forever durable collaboration state with no standing TTL or scheduled deletion path. messages is the canonical local message and dedupe ledger and the startup source for collective-history observation. Collective-history message and observation rows preserve authority and provenance, while delivered replication rows are the durable checkpoint that prevents full replay on every restart. hrcmail_* rows preserve local execution, presentation, reminder, failure-notice, automatic-reply, idempotency, and recovery state around the wrkq-owned collaboration ledger; they do not become room, envelope, obligation, discharge, or reply-body authority. No TTL or delete path for these classes is introduced without separately approved terminality and replay-fence authority.

## hrc-runtime.continuation-history-resume

A non-empty provider continuation key recorded on an HRC session or runtime is durable history: clear, drop, and end operations retain it while recording ordinary fresh-start intent separately as persisted session state. Ordinary run, start, and dispatch recreation suppress automatic continuation reuse while that state is disabled; a later committed continuation.updated enables reuse for its newly recorded key. Explicit hrc resume is status- and clear/drop/terminate-barrier-neutral: it selects the newest recorded key for the normalized target, or the key on a valid pinned session, and fails only when no such key exists or a live-runtime conflict prevents safe reuse. Under the scope-and-lane mint lock, its successor boundary returns a session carrying exactly the selected key with reuse enabled or fails without mutation; a keyless inactive current successor may be bound atomically, a same-key inactive successor may be reused idempotently, and a live or different-key successor conflicts. The read-only session resolve surface exposes retained continuation history independently of automatic-reuse state. Startup repair restores only NULL historical session and runtime keys from each owner's latest non-empty durable broker continuation.updated event, never overwrites a current key, preserves ordinary fresh-start disposition, is idempotent, and completes before request service begins.

## hrc-runtime.harness-broker-admission-client

HRC owns cross-seat scheduling, caller policy, and principal authority while the harness-broker owns per-seat admission mechanism. All HRC broker traffic flows through exactly four class-specific submit methods, one each for steer, queue, exclusive, and preempt; the concrete method names are not law. Admission class is explicit in the method signature and is never selected by a whenBusy parameter; composite behavior such as steer-else-queue is caller composition of typed outcomes. Steer exposes no wait, obligation, or own-response option and resolves only through truthful absorbed or executed disposition. Every obligation-bearing call uses enqueue, invoke, or preempt and originates its own turn; blocking callers correlate by submission disposition and then the identified turn terminal rather than by delivery inference. Preempt requires operator authority or the sender's authority over the envelope driving the active turn, and never arises from a silent class upgrade. HRC consumes broker capability, seat probe, queue, disposition, manifest, and decision-ledger surfaces without reading harness internals or moving per-seat mechanism into the runtime layer. The wrkq mail kicker reads busy state only from the broker-observed seat turn, never from an HRC run row. Ordinary queue-class envelopes arriving during that turn remain in one durable HRC-held batch with no broker submission or wrkq presentation receipt; the terminal turn event, backed by the periodic sweep, freezes and flushes after a second idle-seat observation. Every boundary or idle input contains only envelopes sharing the oldest actionable envelope's exact presentation key: room, sender identity, reply addressee, and fan-out group, up to MAX_PRESENTED_PER_ATTEMPT. Other keys remain held or pending for later turns, and every multi-envelope input has one auto-reply candidate. A competing turn keeps the batch held. Terminal members are removed before prompt composition. An HRC-held member has no broker submission and therefore no broker TTL; only its wrkq sender expiry or withdrawal can terminal it, and flush revalidation honors that ledger state. Once a flush has acquired a broker submission and written per-envelope receipts, a broker queue/submission expiry is logged and fails every receipted member of that shared input as undeliverable so the sender sees a terminal outcome. Each hold/preempt request remains an immediate isolated admission decision and is never batched.

## hrc-runtime.harness-broker-committed-observation-control

HRC observes and projects only committed normalized harness-broker envelopes, and BrokerEventMapper remains their sole interpreter. For each broker sequence, one SQLite transaction idempotently mirrors the normalized envelope, projects runtime run buffer continuation surface and permission state, appends canonical hrc_events, and advances a contiguous projection cursor or records a typed fenced disposition. The cursor advances across intentionally non-mirrored high-volume deltas without treating mirror retention as a source gap. Only after that transaction commits may HRC acknowledge the broker sequence, notify followers, or evaluate a control policy that depends on the fact. HRC is the sole broker-ledger retention-bearing consumer: its fenced control connection owns one durable scalar acknowledgement per invocation, bounded by forensic and active-invocation holds; read-only observer clients have no acknowledgement identity or retention claim and fail typed below the retained floor. This does not change the keep-forever HRC projection law in hrc-runtime.ledger-tool-result-storage. Control attempts remain typed durable intent over the existing specialized stores, and RPC acceptance never proves provider effect; effects return as later committed observations. The wrkq kicker acts only when committed terminal execution truth and authoritative pending-obligation truth agree, no newer input or turn supersedes them, and the one-reminder bound permits the attempt. Explicit policy operator and API permission decisions are HRC-owned and persist before permission.respond on the fenced control connection. A deadline fallback is broker-owned; HRC later projects its already committed permission.resolved timeout fact.

## hrc-runtime.ledger-tool-result-storage

Outside an explicit include-ledgers runtime cascade, broker_invocation_events and hrc_events rows and their tool-result bytes remain keep-forever. HRC removes duplicate envelope payloads and stores every tool result whose serialized value exceeds 32768 UTF-8 bytes once in tool_result_blobs inside state.sqlite, in the same transaction as deterministic excerpt stubs in the ledger rows. Ordinary reads and live notifications hydrate those stubs; only the dedicated federation read paths expose persisted stubs. Federation schedules the local-blob feed before the ledger feeds and transfers blobs using globally unique deterministic identifiers and addressed, idempotently staged parts no larger than 256 KiB; imported blobs are not re-forwarded. A missing or incomplete blob remains observable as its excerpt and increments ledger.blob_miss rather than making its ledger row unreadable. The current authority is the SQLite blob table, without a filesystem carrier, content hash, feature flag, or standing ledger TTL.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-exact-scope-provisioning

Mobile exact-scope provisioning is one implicit reject-on-occupied START with no inbound host session id and a required durable idempotency key. Registry binding remains authoritative for an established scope. For a virgin scope, origin and receiver derive one home in this order: exact pin, exact home, reserved-family home, explicit typed provision.node directive, profile provisioning default, platform default. For an IMPLICIT mail-kicker birth only, when every preceding placement input is silent and the target remains virgin, the registry host may replace the local platform default with one persisted tier-5 birth designation. It derives that designation itself from wrkq's globally earliest reply-required envelope for the target and one registry consult of that envelope's scoped sender: a bound sender contributes its binding home and a retired sender its immutable retired home. The first designation is recorded before response and every later ask returns it unchanged. Only its home may establish with sender-derived provenance; non-homing kickers finish without starting. Every higher-precedence establishment remains admissible and atomically supersedes a live designation. No designation is recorded for no birth envelope or an absent or unbound sender, and inability to consult wrkq or the registry is a typed retryable refusal with no local fallback. A declared roster base reserves its closed suffix namespace on that home, and profile validation rejects pins or homes for reserved members. An explicit node directive is admissible only when no placement declaration applies and is validated at both origin and receiver against the federation registry and the receiver's own profile; conflicts are typed refusals before mutation. No placement is inferred from ambient caller identity, transport, connection, or environment; the mail default is derived only by the registry host from the authoritative ledger envelope and registry state. A remote home is invoked only through the authenticated, capability-advertised exactStart peer verb, whose receiver independently validates retirement, authority, binding, placement, and materialization capability before mutation and localizes runtime intent. On the authoritative home, exact and suffix claim/start share the same roster:<agentId>:<projectId> mutex and FREE predicate, so canonical exact names overlapping suffix members cannot claim one continuity concurrently. A new exact key either atomically rotates or mints a fresh successor, records its canonical request hash, and registers start before releasing the mutex, or returns session_scope_occupied without mutation. Identical retries converge; conflicting replays fail before intent mutation; superseded claims never start archived predecessors. Retryable peer failure is synchronous runtime_unavailable and does not use the message outbox.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-session-index

HRC is the authoritative producer of the Mobile session index: it maintains one current-generation projection per local session lineage; defines recency as the greatest observed contributing activity timestamp; derives effective status and execution mode before reads; and exposes bounded page and facet APIs. Complete federated pages follow the strict order last_activity_at DESC, nodeId ASC, host_session_id DESC through one opaque cursor whose per-node components advance only past emitted rows. Concurrent activity may move a row only toward the head, so a walk has no duplicates or permanent loss; peer failures freeze that peer's component and surface complete:false rather than claiming a complete global interleave. ACP and iOS consume these projections and facets as authoritative and do not acquire peer-probe authority.

## hrc-runtime.mobile-suffix-roster-provisioning

Mobile suffix-roster families are finite. Every enabled ACP quick-pick base has a concrete declared home before the surface is enabled. A declared base reserves every member produced by HRC's fixed ordered suffix list on that home, and profile validation rejects pins or homes for reserved members. An undeclared family may instead use an explicit typed provision.node directive; it is validated at both origin and receiver against the federation registry and the receiver's own profile, and any placement conflict is a typed refusal before mutation. No placement is inferred from caller identity, transport, connection, or environment. Origin HRC routes the whole family from registry binding state and the baseSessionRef-derived family home. A remote home is invoked only through the authenticated, capability-advertised rosterStart peer verb. The receiver independently preflights retirement, authority, binding state, placement, and materialization capability for the whole family before mutation, localizes the runtime intent, and then owns the existing atomic roster claim/start and durable idempotency record. Operator starts without an explicit node directive remain explicit-local. Retryable peer failure is synchronous runtime_unavailable and does not use the message outbox.

## hrc-runtime.observable-release

Every atomic HRC release records its exact HRC build and locked ASP build in praesidium-release.json before cutover; the daemon captures that immutable identity at startup, fails closed for invalid atomic manifests, and reports on every status read whether the running release still equals the installed release. Source and worktree daemons report unmanaged explicitly.

## hrc-runtime.quarantined-release-sweep

Phase 1 quarantine remains reversible and keeps every observed reference. Phase 2 may unlink only valid release-id children of the owning user's .gc-quarantine during an operator-scheduled quiescence window, within the hrc-runtime.quarantined-release-sweep-scan-coherence accepted-risk boundary. Before mutation, the daemon is absent and held down, current-code maintenance and install exclusion is held, the release root and quarantine are owner-owned mode 0700, and two complete clean ps plus privileged open-path observations cover the exact candidate set with an unchanged pid-and-start-time incarnation set. Probe status, output completeness, attestation nonce and candidate scope fail closed. Privilege may actuate supervision and read process state, but every unlink runs as the release owner. Each surviving candidate remains bit-for-bit unmodified on refusal. After all safety gates pass, each candidate transition is ordered: reassert daemon absence, write .sweep-in-progress, recursively set every directory in that candidate to mode 0700, then unlink that same candidate. A sentinel-bearing survivor is non-restorable partial-sweep residue completed by a later successful sweep. Elapsed quarantine age is operator convenience, never evidence of reference absence.

The declared verify gate checks architecture records and their generated projections in addition to build, structural checks, lint, types, tests, and the fixture-owned federation loopback corpus.

## hrc-runtime.viewer-presentation-sidecar

HRC owns runtime lifecycle and the durable presentation facts needed to reconstruct viewer intent, but after viewer cutover it never actuates Ghostty. Each start or reuse publishes runtime.presentation with the invocation-local operator-attach suppression decision, while the runtime generation persists only operator attachability, latest viewer window, and monotone viewerRequested intent. A store-only presentation read model exposes those facts without probing or mutating runtimes. hrc-viewer alone actuates Ghostty through ghostmux and keeps no persistent registry outside Ghostty pane metadata. Raising or focusing an existing pane by a user-principal tool (a CLI the human runs on their own desktop, e.g. hcs) is not presentation actuation for this invariant: it mints, stamps, rebinds, retitles, and closes nothing, and focus is never read for identity or topology decisions. Such a tool may read the pane metadata the viewer wrote to locate a pane; it may not write it. Exactly one viewer-bearing daemon is permitted per GUI user and it is the production daemon; non-production daemons for that user keep their in-daemon Ghostty viewer disabled and never run hrc-viewer. This placement constraint is the authority boundary for the user's shared Ghostty registry; the design does not provide cross-daemon pane ownership or isolation. Within that one viewer, the single global pane for a logical session is keyed by normalized (scopeRef, laneRef), with runtime and generation fences for adoption and reap. A pre-record generation is adopt-only and cannot cause a pane to be minted until an invocation establishes presentation authority. Viewer absence, death, lag, reconnect, reconciliation, and polling cannot mutate or finalize runtime, run, or turn state and cannot delay or fail their lifecycle paths.
